designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Strong, legible deadpan concept: the even-weight icon grid reads as a real dashboard and PROBABLY FINE lands the joke. But it is a tidy spec sheet more than a graphic. Every icon has the same visual weight, the labels are tiny on the tee and fill in at print size, and a few icons are off (the washer fluid, the traction control squiggle). At 3 m it reads as a grey block with a caption.
designs.fix: Push the scale and hierarchy: make the icons bigger with heavier strokes, drop or enlarge the labels, and set PROBABLY FINE big enough to anchor the back, so it reads as a bold graphic and not a manual page.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The best-crafted piece here. The loose brush dogs have real character, the repeated 'Turn around.' pays off with good comic timing, and the italic serif gives it a quiet, giftable tone. Weaknesses: the art is thin-lined and placed small, so it disappears on the tee at distance; step 5's pose is muddy; and 6 and 7 are near-twins, which slightly flattens the ending.
designs.fix: Enlarge the whole lockup about 25% and thicken the brush strokes so the dogs hold up on black, and make the step-5 spin pose read more clearly as mid-turn.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Clean, confident line work and the tabby is well drawn. But the cat-prefers-the-box gag is one of the most worn jokes in pet merch, and the three stacked panels make a narrow strip that looks skinny and undersized on the back. Panel 2 doesn't stage 'ignores it' clearly: the cat stares at the viewer while a hand still holds the bed. The odd flag-shaped '1' and the frame-breaking box and bed feel accidental, not designed.
designs.fix: Redesign panel 2 so the cat clearly turns its back on the offered bed, and widen the layout (larger panels, numerals sized to the art) so it fills the back with a real presence.
